Async functions, awaits and promises. The harness settles the promises later, laterText and failLater make once
main returns, in the order they were made.

=== an async function that doesn't wait settles its promise at once, and awaiting it goes on at once
-- script/main --
import { log } from "test"
async function two(): Promise<number> { return 2 }
async function run(): Promise<void> {
  const x = await two()
  log("got " + str(x))
}
export function main(): number {
  run()
  log("after run")
  return 1
}
-- want --
1
-- logs --
got 2
after run

=== awaits wait for the host, and go on in the order their promises settle
-- script/main --
import { log, later } from "test"
async function wait(name: string, v: number): Promise<void> {
  log(name + " waits")
  const [x, err] = await later(v)
  log(name + " got " + str(x) + " " + str(err == null))
}
export function main(): number {
  wait("a", 1)
  wait("b", 2)
  log("main ends")
  return 0
}
-- logs --
a waits
b waits
main ends
a got 1 true
b got 2 true

=== an error is a value: the host's, passed on, and taken apart
-- script/main --
import { log, failLater, ProbeError } from "test"
async function load(): Promise<number, ProbeError> {
  const [x, err] = await failLater("empty")
  if (err != null) {
    return err
  }
  return x
}
async function run(): Promise<void> {
  const [v, err] = await load()
  log(str(v) + " " + err.code)
}
export function main(): number {
  run()
  return 0
}
-- logs --
0 empty

=== a script's own error class, and a subclass of it
-- script/main --
import { log, later } from "test"
error class ShopError {
  code: string
  constructor(code: string) { this.code = code }
}
error class Closed extends ShopError {
  constructor() { super("closed") }
}
async function buy(gold: number): Promise<string, ShopError> {
  const [have, _] = await later(gold)
  if (have < 0) {
    return new Closed()
  }
  if (have < 10) {
    return new ShopError("poor")
  }
  return "sword"
}
async function run(): Promise<void> {
  const [a, e1] = await buy(5)
  log(a + "|" + e1.code)
  const [b, e2] = await buy(20)
  log(b + "|" + str(e2 == null))
  const [c, e3] = await buy(-1)
  log(c + "|" + e3.code)
}
export function main(): number {
  run()
  return 0
}
-- logs --
|poor
sword|true
|closed

=== loops keep their variables across awaits: for … of with continue and break, and while
-- script/main --
import { log, later } from "test"
async function sum(xs: number[]): Promise<number> {
  let total = 0
  for (const x of xs) {
    if (x < 0) {
      continue
    }
    const [v, _] = await later(x)
    total += v
    if (total > 10) {
      break
    }
  }
  return total
}
async function count(n: number): Promise<number> {
  let i = 0
  let s = ""
  while (i < n) {
    const [v, _] = await later(i)
    s += str(v)
    i++
  }
  log(s)
  return i
}
async function run(): Promise<void> {
  const total = await sum([1, -5, 2, 3, 20, 4])
  log("total " + str(total))
  const n = await count(4)
  log("count " + str(n))
}
export function main(): number {
  run()
  return 0
}
-- logs --
total 26
0123
count 4

=== branches with awaits in both, nested in a loop
-- script/main --
import { log, later, laterText } from "test"
async function run(): Promise<void> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    if (i % 2 == 0) {
      const [v, _] = await later(i * 10)
      log("even " + str(v))
    } else {
      const s = await laterText("odd")
      log(s + " " + str(i))
    }
  }
}
export function main(): number {
  run()
  return 0
}
-- logs --
even 0
odd 1
even 20

=== async methods keep this, and return await passes a promise's outcome on
-- script/main --
import { log, later, failLater, ProbeError } from "test"
class Counter {
  n = 0
  async add(v: number): Promise<number, ProbeError> {
    const [x, err] = await later(v)
    if (err != null) {
      return err
    }
    this.n += x
    return this.n
  }
  async broken(): Promise<number, ProbeError> {
    return await failLater("broken")
  }
}
async function run(): Promise<void> {
  const c = new Counter()
  const [a, _] = await c.add(2)
  const [b, _e] = await c.add(3)
  log(str(a) + " " + str(b) + " " + str(c.n))
  const [x, err] = await c.broken()
  log(str(x) + " " + err.code)
}
export function main(): number {
  run()
  return 0
}
-- logs --
2 5 5
0 broken

=== assignments take what an await gives
-- script/main --
import { log, later, laterText, ProbeError } from "test"
class Box {
  text = ""
  n = 0
  err: ProbeError = null
}
async function run(): Promise<void> {
  const b = new Box()
  b.text = await laterText("hi")
  [b.n, b.err] = await later(7)
  log(b.text + " " + str(b.n) + " " + str(b.err == null))
}
export function main(): number {
  run()
  return 0
}
-- logs --
hi 7 true

=== a promise kept in a field, awaited twice, and awaited after it settled
-- script/main --
import { log, laterText } from "test"
class Holder {
  p: Promise<string> = null
}
async function first(h: Holder): Promise<void> {
  const s = await h.p
  log("first " + s)
}
async function second(h: Holder): Promise<void> {
  const s = await h.p
  log("second " + s)
  const again = await h.p
  log("again " + again)
}
export function main(): number {
  const h = new Holder()
  h.p = laterText("x")
  first(h)
  second(h)
  return 0
}
-- logs --
first x
second x
again x

=== a promise that can't fail goes where one may fail
-- script/main --
import { log, ProbeError } from "test"
async function one(): Promise<number> { return 1 }
function pass(): Promise<number, ProbeError> { return one() }
async function run(): Promise<void> {
  const [v, err] = await pass()
  log(str(v) + " " + str(err == null))
}
export function main(): number {
  run()
  return 0
}
-- logs --
1 true

=== an async method stands for an optional method the host calls
-- script/main --
import { log, later, Hooks } from "test"
class H implements Hooks {
  async ready(): Promise<void> {
    await later(1)
    log("ready")
  }
  run(): void {}
}
export function main(): number {
  const h = new H()
  h.ready()
  return 0
}
-- logs --
ready

=== a failure after an await fails the call that resumed it
-- script/main --
import { later } from "test"
async function boom(): Promise<void> {
  const [x, _] = await later(0)
  const y = 1 / x
}
export function main(): number {
  boom()
  return 0
}
-- eval error --
division by zero

=== awaiting null fails
-- script/main --
async function run(): Promise<void> {
  const p: Promise<number> = null
  const x = await p
}
export function main(): number {
  run()
  return 0
}
-- eval error --
await of null

=== await is only in async functions
-- script/main --
import { later } from "test"
export function main(): number {
  const [x, _] = await later(1)
  return x
}
-- compile error --
await is only in async functions

=== a promise that may fail is taken apart
-- script/main --
import { later } from "test"
async function run(): Promise<void> {
  const x = await later(1)
}
export function main(): number { return 0 }
-- compile error --
may fail with ProbeError: take both

=== a promise that can't fail isn't
-- script/main --
async function one(): Promise<number> { return 1 }
async function run(): Promise<void> {
  const [x, err] = await one()
}
export function main(): number { return 0 }
-- compile error --
can't fail: take its value alone

=== await isn't part of an expression
-- script/main --
import { log } from "test"
async function two(): Promise<number> { return 2 }
async function run(): Promise<void> {
  log(str(await two()))
}
export function main(): number { return 0 }
-- compile error --
await can't be part of an expression

=== await isn't in a for loop's header
-- script/main --
async function two(): Promise<number> { return 2 }
async function run(): Promise<void> {
  for (let i = await two(); i < 3; i++) {}
}
export function main(): number { return 0 }
-- compile error --
await can't be in a for loop's header

=== a promise fails with an error class
-- script/main --
async function run(): Promise<number, string> { return 1 }
export function main(): number { return 0 }
-- compile error --
a promise fails with an error class

=== a promise's value isn't an error class
-- script/main --
error class E {}
async function run(): Promise<E> { return new E() }
export function main(): number { return 0 }
-- compile error --
is an error class: a promise fails with it

=== an error class extends only error classes
-- script/main --
class Plain {}
error class E extends Plain {}
export function main(): number { return 0 }
-- compile error --
an error class extends only error classes

=== a plain class doesn't extend an error class
-- script/main --
error class E {}
class Plain extends E {}
export function main(): number { return 0 }
-- compile error --
only an error class extends it

=== an async function returns a promise
-- script/main --
async function run(): number { return 1 }
export function main(): number { return 0 }
-- compile error --
an async function returns a Promise

=== an async function returns its promise's value
-- script/main --
async function run(): Promise<number> { return true }
export function main(): number { return 0 }
-- compile error --
run returns a number, not a bool

=== a promise that can't fail isn't rejected
-- script/main --
error class E {}
async function run(): Promise<number> { return new E() }
export function main(): number { return 0 }
-- compile error --
run's promise can't fail

=== it fails only with its own error class
-- script/main --
error class E {}
error class F {}
async function run(): Promise<number, E> { return new F() }
export function main(): number { return 0 }
-- compile error --
run fails with E, not F

=== a promise that may fail doesn't go where one can't
-- script/main --
import { later } from "test"
function f(): Promise<number> { return later(1) }
export function main(): number { return 0 }
-- compile error --
f returns a Promise<number>, not a Promise<number, ProbeError>

=== an async method stands only for an optional method
-- script/main --
import { Hooks } from "test"
class H implements Hooks {
  async run(): Promise<void> {}
}
export function main(): number { return 0 }
-- compile error --
H doesn't implement Hooks: run is (): Promise<void>, not (): void

=== a host waits for at most 64 promises at a time
-- script/main --
import { later, ProbeError } from "test"
export function main(): number {
  const ps: Promise<number, ProbeError>[] = []
  for (let i = 0; i < 65; i++) {
    ps.push(later(i))
  }
  return ps.length
}
-- eval error --
more than 64 promises
